items.description:
Cosy Corner is a halaal takeaway and casual dining spot in Wynberg, serving Cape Malay-style food to local families and visitors who want a quick, affordable meal. The menu runs from gatsbys and hotdogs to flame-grilled chicken, rib-eye steaks, lamb chops and seafood, alongside steak sandwiches, chips and milkshakes, all prepared without alcohol on the premises.

The business has traded from the same part of Wynberg since 1973, giving it more than fifty years of history in the area, and it still runs primarily as a takeaway counter rather than a sit-down restaurant. It suits customers after a fast, no-frills halaal meal rather than a formal dining experience, and its long run in Wynberg has made it a familiar stop for generations of local diners. The shop trades from 119 Ottery Road in Wynberg, Cape Town.

items.description:
Faeeza's Home Kitchen is a Cape Malay cooking school and restaurant run from a home on the corner of a courtyard in the heart of Bo-Kaap, Cape Town. The hostess grew up in Bo-Kaap eating Cape Malay dishes her mother cooked, and although her mother never taught her exact recipes, she knew how they were meant to taste.

Her cooking and catering journey began 25 years ago with a sandwich kiosk at the University of Cape Town, and it has grown over the decades into the home kitchen and cooking classes run today. Guests learn to cook authentic Cape Malay dishes themselves, alongside hearing stories about the culture, the neighbourhood and the journey that led here. It suits visitors who want a hands-on cooking experience and a genuine taste of Bo-Kaap's food culture.

For the Love of Silk supplies premium silk textiles for fashion designers, creative professionals and anyone planning a bespoke garment, stocking silk satin, silk chiffon, crepe de chine, silk georgette and other silk fabrics by the metre. Alongside the fabric range, the business sells finished silk products for everyday living, including printed silk scarves made from its own textiles.

Its showroom at Cape Quarter Lifestyle Village on Somerset Road is open by appointment, allowing customers to handle and compare fabrics before committing to a design. The business suits dressmakers, bridal and evening-wear designers and private customers who want a specific silk weight or finish rather than a generic fabric-shop range. Shop 30 in Cape Quarter Lifestyle Village serves as its base in Cape Town.

Glen Country Club is a private sporting and social club in Clifton, built around tennis courts and lawn bowls, with three separate bowling greens for members and visiting teams. Alongside regular club sport, the venue is set up to host private and corporate functions, making it both a sports facility and an events space.

Founded in 1955, the club sits within the Clifton scenic reserve close to Clifton Beach, a setting that has shaped its character as a long-standing social institution rather than a purely competitive sports club. For members and visitors who want a sporting or social base on the Atlantic Seaboard, Glen Country Club also runs a second venue in Green Point able to accommodate larger group bookings.

Ground Art Caffe is a coffee bar and micro-gallery on Strand Street in De Waterkant, combining quality espresso with a changing display of local artwork on its gallery wall. The café serves breakfast, lunch and brunch alongside its coffee menu, with a dedicated barista pulling the espresso and an in-house curator responsible for the rotating exhibitions.

Orders are placed and collected at the counter rather than served to a table, and takeaway food comes packaged in eco-friendly boxes and bags. Free wifi is available for customers who want to linger over a coffee. The combination of café and gallery under one roof suits coffee drinkers and art enthusiasts alike, and the business trades from 160 Strand Street in De Waterkant.

items.description:
HCI, or Hosken Consolidated Investments, is a black empowerment investment holding company listed on the JSE under the share code HCI, in the Diversified Financial Services sector. Its major shareholder is the South African Clothing and Textile Workers Union, and the group has a branch at The Point in Sea Point, Cape Town.

The group holds a diverse spread of investments spanning hotels and leisure, interactive gaming, media and broadcasting, transport, mining and properties. HCI publishes its annual, interim and financial reports for investors, and it maintains stakes in companies across these different industries rather than operating in just one sector. It suits investors and stakeholders who want to understand the scope of HCI's diversified investment portfolio.

items.description:
Hybrid Composite designs and manufactures equipment for the superyacht and wider marine industry, producing flush deck hatches, companionway and crew-access entrances, emergency escape systems, saloon windows and other marine hardware and seals. Its work extends to full yacht interior fittings, giving boatyards and builders a single supplier for both structural access equipment and finishing components.

The company was founded in Cape Town in 2008 and has built its process around 3D CAD modelling, detailed design, CNC cutting, composite prototyping, acrylic machining and project management, covering a project from concept through to a finished part. It suits superyacht builders and boatyards needing standard, semi-custom or fully custom equipment rather than off-the-shelf components. The workshop operates from Unit 7, 7 Inyoni Street in Ndabeni, Cape Town.

Innohealth Medical Centres Mitchells Plain is a medical centre at 6 Woolworths Arcade Building in Mitchells Plain Town Centre, Cape Town, and it was the group's first Innohealth location. The practice offers primary care, with doctors available for consultations and bookings taken by phone or WhatsApp.

Most medical aids are accepted, and cash rates are listed for consultations, including a standard rate, a student rate and a pensioner rate, all of which include basic medication. The practice also runs an Innohealth Plus membership at a set monthly fee, along with managed care programmes for people with chronic conditions. It suits residents of Mitchells Plain who want affordable GP consultations with clear, published pricing.

Ixia Street Animal Hospital is a veterinary hospital in Milnerton, Cape Town, established for 18 years and well equipped for modern veterinary care. Its services cover hospitalisation, sterilisations, nutritional services, check-ups, vaccinations and dental services, alongside medical, surgical and high-care treatment.

The hospital's own site sums up its approach as love is the best medicine, with doctors and staff committed to providing up-to-date, caring, professional and efficient care for cats, dogs and other small pets. It suits pet owners in Milnerton who want a long-established, well-equipped hospital for routine and more involved veterinary care. Pet owners can call the hospital directly to book an appointment or discuss a concern about their animal's health.

Jack Black Brewing Company is an independently owned and operated craft brewery based in Diep River, producing beer that has grown into one of South Africa's more established craft brands. The Diep River site combines the working brewery with a year-round taproom, where visitors can sample both long-running favourites and newer, limited-edition batches.

The taproom also runs a simple food menu alongside the beer, a small retail shop for take-home purchases, and brewery tours that can be booked by appointment for a behind-the-scenes look at how the beer is made. It suits beer drinkers and visitors wanting a tasting experience rather than just a bottle shop, in a space built around the brewery's own production. The business has operated from Diep River, Cape Town, since 2016.

Jakes is a restaurant group with locations in Tokai and Noordhoek, Cape Town, serving global, social food for more than three decades. The Tokai branch, known as Jakes in the Village, is part of a brand that describes itself as where Cape Town comes to unwind, with alfresco lunches, lively dinners and cocktails paired with local wines and craft beers on tap.

The restaurants run from lazy weekend breakfasts through to after-work gatherings, built around a passionate team of chefs, managers and front-of-house staff. Trading hours run from 11h30 to 22h30 on weekdays, from 9am on Saturdays, and from 9am to 5pm on Sundays, though times may vary. It suits groups who want a relaxed, social meal with a wide drinks selection in Tokai.

JAM Clothing is a national discount fashion retailer with a branch at Gugulethu Square in Gugulethu, Cape Town. The brand positions itself as famous for less, offering clothing for ladies, men, girls and boys alongside in-store promotions.

The Gugulethu Square store trades Monday to Thursday from 09:00 to 18:00, Fridays until 19:00, Saturdays from 09:00 to 17:00, and Sundays and public holidays from 09:00 to 15:00. The brand also runs a JAM Cares programme as part of its wider community work. It suits shoppers in Gugulethu who want affordable, everyday clothing for the whole family.

items.description:
Kenwyn Martial Arts Centre has offered instruction and training in Karate since 2001, based at 19 Civic Road in Kenwyn, Cape Town. The directory listing describing the dojo notes it also runs health and fitness holiday activities for kids, alongside its core martial arts programme.

The centre's listing places it under both martial arts and child-focused sports coaching and training categories, reflecting classes that run for both adults and children. Customers can request a quote or booking, or contact the centre directly through its directory listing. It suits families in Kenwyn looking for Karate instruction or holiday activity programmes for children.

Kristen's Kick-Ass Ice Cream is an artisanal ice cream parlour in Newlands, making handmade flavours on site that range from signature favourites to rotating seasonal batches. Dietary options are built into the regular range rather than offered as an afterthought, with vegan, dairy-free and sugar-free scoops alongside flavours such as vanilla bean, salted caramel, coffee and dark chocolate, and pistachio.

A vegan coconut fudge flavour sits among the current line-up, reflecting a menu that keeps changing rather than sticking to a fixed list. The Newlands shop, at Cardiff Castle on Main Street, is open Monday to Thursday until 8pm and stays open later, until half past nine, from Friday through the weekend. It suits families and customers with dietary restrictions who still want a full range of flavours to choose from.

L'Atelier Optometrist is an optometry practice in Cape Quarter, De Waterkant, offering a full range of eye care from comprehensive eye examinations and children's vision assessments to contact lens consultations, dry-eye assessments, myopia management, diabetic eye screening and glaucoma screening. Retinal imaging is used as part of these assessments, alongside advanced diagnostic technology in the practice's own consulting rooms.

Beyond eye examinations, the practice supplies prescription eyewear and premium lenses, and it participates in the Discovery Health Optometry Network, making claims more straightforward for members on that scheme. With more than twenty years of experience behind it, the practice suits adults and children needing anything from a routine eye test to ongoing management of a specific eye condition. It trades from Shop 25 in Cape Quarter Lifestyle Village on Somerset Road.

Lotus River Primary School is a public primary school in the Southern Suburbs area of the City of Cape Town, on the corner of Lake Road and 5th Avenue in Lotus River. The school has 595 learners and 20 educators, giving a learner-to-educator ratio of close to 30 to 1.

This ratio, which divides total learners by the number of educators, gives a sense of class sizes at the school relative to its teaching staff. It suits families in Lotus River who want a public primary school serving the local community. The information comes from a schools directory that tracks learner and educator numbers for public schools across the province.

items.description:
Miller's Thumb Restaurant is a seafood restaurant in Gardens, trading from a converted home that keeps its original cosy, character-filled feel rather than a purpose-built dining room. The kitchen builds its menu around fresh seafood, including fish, crustaceans and calamari, and extends into seafood curries carrying Asian and spicy influences rather than a plain grill-and-fry approach.

The restaurant has operated on Kloof Nek Road since the 1990s, making it one of the longer-running seafood addresses in the area, and it offers both sit-down dining and pavement pick-ups for those in a hurry. Dinner service runs most evenings, with a shorter lunch service served on weekdays. It suits diners who want a seafood-focused menu with a bit more spice and variety than a typical fish restaurant.

Mitchells Plain Oral Health Centre is a public dental and oral health facility run by the Western Cape Department of Health, based on the 6th floor of the Melomed Mitchells Plain building on Symphony Walk. It offers dental and oral health services to patients from Mitchells Plain and the surrounding communities rather than operating as a private practice.

The facility keeps standard weekday hours, opening each morning and closing in the late afternoon from Monday to Friday. It suits patients who need public dental care in the area and are referred to or walk in at this specific government-run clinic rather than a private dentist. Its location inside the Melomed building places it alongside the hospital's other medical services.

Mungo High Constantia is the brand's fourth retail store, opened on 3 October 2020 under the leafy oaks of the High Constantia Shopping Centre in Constantia, Cape Town. The company describes it as Mungo Cape Town's little sister store, sitting alongside other boutique stores and artisanal eateries in the Southern Suburbs.

The store stocks the brand's full range of natural fibre homeware textiles, from everyday classics to contemporary additions for the bath, bed, kitchen and table. Shoppers can browse, touch and try the products firsthand, including trying one of the brand's signature flat-weave towels at the basin, and staff on hand can explain the historic techniques and tools behind the range. It suits homeware shoppers who want to feel the quality of natural fibre textiles before buying.

Nando's Grassy Park is a drive-thru branch of the flame-grilled PERi-PERi chicken chain, serving Portuguese-inspired grilled meals to residents and visitors in the area. The branch is set up for drive-through as well as dine-in, so customers can choose a sit-down meal or grab food without leaving their car.

Takeaway, collection and delivery are also available alongside the drive-through lane, giving the branch more ways to order than a typical dine-in-only restaurant. It suits families and commuters along Prince George Drive who want a quick peri-peri meal on the way past rather than a sit-down occasion. The branch trades from the corner of Prince George Drive and 5th Avenue in Grassy Park.

Ndoro is a craft shop in Noordhoek Farm Village, Cape Town, trading in summer from 08:30 to 17:30 and in winter from 09:00 to 17:00. A Cape Town Magazine feature describes it as small and sweet, in contrast to the huge, overwhelming selection found at some African arts and crafts shops.

The shop's well-chosen selection includes ceramics, clay animals, baskets, wall decorations, maps, crockery, jewellery and fabrics, sourced as handmade African products for the home. It suits shoppers at Noordhoek Farm Village who want a curated, manageable selection of African crafts rather than an overwhelming one.

Norma-Jean's Beauty Salon and Tattoo Parlor offers a range of beauty treatments in Kuils River, including hair removal, facials and general skincare alongside makeup application and eyebrow threading. Body sculpting treatments are also part of the regular menu, giving the salon a broader beauty offering than a salon focused only on hair or nails.

Tattoo work is available alongside the beauty side of the business, reflected in its name and giving customers a single address for both services. The salon trades Tuesday to Friday from 8am to 6pm and Saturdays from 8am to 3pm, closed on Mondays and Sundays. It suits customers in Kuils River looking for skincare, beauty or cosmetic treatments without needing to travel further afield.

items.description:
NV-80 Grill & Bar is a grill-house restaurant at The Point in Sea Point, built around steaks, seafood and salads alongside a changing line-up of starters, sides and daily specials. The menu reflects an older style of grill-house cooking, reworked for a more contemporary dining room rather than a retro throwback.

Alongside its main dining area, the restaurant has a private dining area and an outside veranda, giving it space for private functions as well as everyday walk-in meals. Now run by a hospitality group that took over the brand in 2022, it has built a reputation as an established Cape Town grill-house over the years. The restaurant trades from Shop 08 on the first floor of The Point in Sea Point.

Oakhurst Farmstall Kenilworth is a farm stall and deli at 284A Main Road in Kenilworth, Cape Town, independently owned and not a subsidiary of the Oakhurst farmstall in Hout Bay. The farmstall trades Monday to Friday from 8:30am to 5:30pm and Saturdays from 8:30am to 2pm, while its coffee shop keeps slightly shorter hours on weekdays and Saturdays.

The business supplies a large range of hot foods for dinner parties, and customers can place a special order with the deli, including having meals prepared in their own dishes for a personal touch. Oakhurst says it takes pride in the quality of the products and produce it supplies to customers. It suits customers who want fresh deli food, confectionery and prepared meals for entertaining.

Olympia Cafe and Deli is an all-day café, bakery and deli in Kalk Bay, serving breakfast, lunch and dinner alongside its own bakery counter and coffee menu. The kitchen leans on seafood and Mediterranean-influenced dishes, and the business also runs occasional functions and jazz evenings alongside its regular café service.

The café follows a stated set of house practices, including using free-range chicken and duck in its pies and sandwiches, serving only filtered water, and packaging orders in biodegradable cups and straws rather than single-use plastic. It suits residents and visitors wanting a relaxed, all-day meal with a deli and bakery attached, rather than a formal sit-down restaurant alone. The business trades from 134 Main Road, on the corner of Windsor and Main Roads in Kalk Bay.

Peacock Tea & Coffee is a proudly South African company based in Cape Town, established in 1966, with a branch in Rondebosch Main Centre. Over nearly 60 years, the company has become one of South Africa's most well-established suppliers of premium teas and coffees.

The business operates as a coffee and tea wholesaler as well as a retailer, and it runs wholesale training and technical services alongside its wholesale products for trade customers. Its stores page lists multiple branches across the Cape, including one in Noordhoek. It suits customers who want freshly ground coffee and a wide range of teas from a long-established South African supplier.

PEP Home Durbanville Town Centre is a homeware and household goods store trading from Shop 6 inside Durbanville Town Centre on Wellington Street. As part of the national PEP Home chain, the branch stocks furniture, bedding and other everyday home essentials at the value pricing the brand is known for, giving shoppers an affordable option for smaller home purchases.

It suits households looking for furniture and bedding without a trip to a larger furniture showroom, picking up smaller home items alongside a weekly shop at the centre. The branch forms part of the wider Durbanville Town Centre retail mix, making it an easy stop for shoppers already there for groceries or other errands, and a convenient option for last-minute home needs.

items.description:
Rain operates a store inside Cape Quarter Lifestyle Village, trading in the centre's Audio & Electronics section alongside other mobile and electronics retailers. The store sells the network's mobile and home internet connectivity products, including SIM cards and devices for customers who want uncapped data without a fixed-line connection.

It suits residents and businesses in and around De Waterkant who want to sign up for a mobile or home internet plan in person rather than online, with staff on hand to help choose a suitable device or package. The store forms a small but practical part of the centre's retail mix alongside its fashion, food and lifestyle tenants.

Rheinmetall Denel Munition is jointly owned by Rheinmetall Waffe Munition GmbH of Germany, which holds 51 percent, and Denel of South Africa, with its South African head office in Somerset West, near Firgrove, Cape Town. The company specialises in the development, design and manufacture of large- and medium-calibre ammunition families.

It is a world leader in artillery, mortar and infantry systems as well as plant engineering. While Rheinmetall's wider business is mainly focused on NATO countries, Rheinmetall Denel Munition's own focus is on Asia, the Middle East, South America, South Africa and other African countries. It suits readers wanting background on the ownership and specialisation of this defence manufacturing joint venture.

Richelles Wedding Dresses is a bridal boutique in Durbanville with a collection of more than one hundred wedding dresses available for brides to try on in person. Alongside the ready collection, the business offers both dress hire and custom-designed gowns, built around personalised attention for each bride rather than an off-the-rack approach.

Appointments are arranged directly with the boutique, which trades on weekdays from 9am to 8pm and on Saturdays from 9am to 6pm. It suits brides who want a wide range of styles to try alongside the option of a gown made specifically for them, with enough time set aside at each appointment to find the right fit. The boutique is based at 5 Amelia Street in Amanda Glen, Durbanville.

Savoy Lodge is a guesthouse in Rondebosch East offering en-suite rooms with their own bathrooms, air-conditioning, wifi and a kitchenette, along with a work desk for guests who need to get things done while travelling. An outdoor pool and jacuzzi are available on site, giving guests somewhere to unwind between outings.

The property also has an event space that can take larger groups, alongside a paid airport shuttle service for guests arriving without their own transport. It suits short-stay visitors and travellers who want a self-contained room with its own kitchenette rather than a standard hotel room, plus the option of a group booking for an event. The lodge is based at 86 Kromboom Road and 3rd Avenue in Rondebosch East.

items.description:
Silulo Ulutho Technologies is a technology outlet with a branch in Town 1 Village 1, Khayelitsha, part of a company established in 2004 that describes its mission as bridging the digital divide through accessible technology education and community empowerment. The company offers computer training, internet access, printing services, CV writing and business ICT support from its branches across the Eastern and Western Cape.

Its online courses let learners develop practical workplace skills, including short, focused two-week programmes such as a course for aspiring petrol attendants, priced at R500 each. The group says its services are designed to uplift individuals and small businesses through comprehensive ICT support. It suits residents of Khayelitsha who want computer access, training or help with a CV close to home.

Site B Youth Clinic is a City of Cape Town public health facility in Khayelitsha, focused on primary healthcare for young people in Site B and the surrounding community. Services at the clinic include family planning, HIV testing and care, and the assessment and treatment of sexually transmitted infections.

It suits young residents who want accessible primary healthcare close to home rather than travelling to a larger hospital for routine or sexual health services. The clinic is run as part of the City's network of public health facilities rather than as a private practice. It is based on the corner of Pama and Lwandle Road in Site B, Khayelitsha.

Spaces Century City is a coworking and flexible office centre in the Bridgeways Precinct, offering private offices, dedicated desks and meeting rooms for businesses and individuals who need a flexible base rather than a long-term lease. The centre is set up for freelancers, entrepreneurs and remote workers alongside larger teams needing dedicated office space.

Members with private offices or dedicated desks get 24-hour access to the building, allowing work outside standard office hours when needed. It suits companies and individuals who want a ready-to-use workspace with meeting rooms on hand for client visits, without managing their own office lease. The centre is based at 1 Bridgeway Road in the Bridgeways Precinct, Century City.

Starlings Locale is a café and restaurant in a residential part of Claremont, serving breakfast and lunch built around fresh produce alongside its coffee and light bakery items. It operates as a sister venue to Starlings Café, carrying a similar focus on specialty coffee into a second, more neighbourhood-feeling location.

The venue offers both indoor and outdoor seating, with the outdoor tables taking in mountain views rather than a busy street scene. It suits local residents after a casual breakfast or lunch stop rather than visitors looking for a central Claremont address, with the coffee and food pitched at an everyday rather than special-occasion level. The café trades from 4 Mark Road in Claremont.

The Brasserie is a French-Italian restaurant at Shop 1, Forest Glade House on Tokai Road in Tokai, Cape Town, dedicated to good food and friends. The restaurant describes itself as Tokai's best-kept culinary secret, blending French flair with Italian soul in a relaxed setting that feels like home.

It suits a casual lunch, a romantic dinner or a special celebration, with its unpretentious charm and warmth setting the tone for each visit. The restaurant trades Monday to Friday from 12:00 to 23:00, Saturdays from 09:00 to 23:00, and Sundays from 09:00 to 16:00, with last orders taken shortly before closing. Guests can book a table by phone or through secure online reservations. It suits diners in Tokai who want a relaxed neighbourhood restaurant with a French-Italian menu.

items.description:
The Little Fisherman is a fresh fish and seafood shop at Shop 11, Dean Street Arcade in Newlands, Cape Town. Customers can contact the business directly to place a fish order ahead of collection, according to its contact page.

The shop trades Monday to Friday from 08:30 to 18:00 and Saturdays from 08:30 to 15:00, closed on Sundays. It suits customers in Newlands who want fresh fish and prawns, with staff available to help prepare the catch before it goes home. The arcade location makes it an easy stop alongside other shops in Dean Street while running other errands in Newlands.

The Live Edge is a furniture studio at The Old Biscuit Mill in Woodstock, Cape Town, creating bespoke, one-of-a-kind live edge tables and decor. The studio uses sustainably sourced wood to make both straight and live-edge tables, with designs built around the natural beauty found in the timber itself.

The natural edge of each piece, along with the patterns and imperfections that occur naturally within the wood grain, are brought out through the studio's meticulous workmanship. Tables can be customised with a choice of legs and bases to suit a customer's space and needs, with what the studio describes as infinite combinations and ideas. It suits customers who want a one-of-a-kind table or decor piece made from sustainably sourced timber.

The Real Repair Company is a device repair business with a branch in Gardens Shopping Centre, fixing smartphones, tablets and smartwatches from brands including Apple, Samsung and Huawei. Repairs are generally completed within about an hour, letting customers wait for a fix rather than leaving a device behind for days.

Work carried out at the branch comes with a parts-and-labour guarantee, giving customers some cover if a repair does not hold. It suits shoppers who crack a screen or damage a device and want it fixed while they are already at the centre, rather than booking in elsewhere and waiting for a courier service. The branch trades from Shop 36A on Mill Street inside Gardens Shopping Centre.

Tile Factory Shop, trading as Kales Tiles, is a tile retailer in Paarden Eiland, Cape Town. The business says customers owe it to themselves to compare its price, quality, range and service before buying elsewhere, offering a wide range of products including tiles, mosaics, cement pavers, brick tiles, cladding and paint.

Its selection of ceramic and porcelain tiles is large and regularly restocked, which the business says makes it impractical to keep a catalogue; customers are invited to visit its two stores to find the right tile for their project. Wall tiles range in size from 200x500mm up to 350x350mm, with floor tiles available in a range of sizes too. It suits homeowners and builders who want to compare tile options in person before choosing for a renovation or new build.
